processing: Orthodox Darjeeling processing for its black teas, with lighter oxidation in spring as is usual; the garden also makes green and speciality teas.
harvest_season: First flush, second flush and autumn are the pickings the garden is known for, along with clonal lots.
appearance_dry: Typical of Darjeeling, twisted olive-and-brown leaf with pale tips, with clonal spring lots often greener.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold in first flush, amber in second flush and autumn.
appearance_wet: Green-and-copper leaf in spring, browner in summer and autumn.
taste_profile: As is typical for the district, floral and brisk in first flush, rounder and fruitier in second flush and autumn.

brewing.notes: Western-style. Use about 85°C for first flush and clonal lots, and hotter water for autumn.

vintage_note: Sold by year and flush, with clonal lots named as such; autumn tea appears later in the year. First flush is best within about a year. Check flush and any clonal label, since they give very different cups from the same garden.
description:
Singbulli is one of the larger Darjeeling gardens, spread over nine rolling hills in the Mirik block. Its 473.95 cultivated hectares run from 1,200 to 4,100 feet, low for Darjeeling, and are split into four divisions: Singbulli, Manja, Tingling and Murmah.

The garden makes about 250 tonnes a year, black tea along with green and speciality lots. Its clonal teas and its first flush, second flush and autumn pickings are the ones with a name.

Brew it like other Darjeelings, with cooler water for spring and clonal lots. Because the altitude range is so wide, two Singbulli lots can differ a lot, so taste before buying in quantity.

A useful comparison is a Singbulli first flush against one from a higher garden such as Sungma, to see what altitude does in the cup.
history: British planters established Singbulli in 1924, making it a relatively late arrival among Darjeeling gardens. Manjushree Tea and India Pvt Ltd, of the Berlia family, took it over in 2020.
